properties.name: Garden of Eden (Theory 1: Armenian Highlands)
properties.description: Egyptologist David Rohl proposes Eden was near Tabriz, Iran, where four rivers converge from the Armenian highlands.
properties.debate: This theory places Eden at the headwaters where Tigris and Euphrates originate, with Pishon and Gihon as other regional rivers.

properties.name: Garden of Eden (Theory 2: Southern Mesopotamia)
properties.description: Traditional view places Eden in southern Iraq where Tigris and Euphrates converge before emptying into Persian Gulf.
properties.debate: Ancient Sumerians called this region 'Dilmun' - a paradise. Pre-Flood geography may have been drastically different.

properties.name: Tigris River (Hiddekel)
properties.description: The Tigris (Hebrew: Hiddekel) flows east of Assyria. One of the four rivers flowing from Eden.
properties.archaeology: The Tigris remains one of the major rivers of Mesopotamia, supporting the region's identification with Eden.

properties.name: Euphrates River
properties.description: The Euphrates is the only river named without further description, suggesting it was well-known to the original audience.

properties.name: Land of Havilah (Pishon River Region)
properties.popup: DISPUTED: Land of gold and bdellium - Genesis 2:11-12
properties.description: The Pishon flowed around Havilah, known for gold, bdellium, and onyx. Some identify this with Arabia or the dried Wadi Batin.
properties.debate: Satellite imagery reveals a dried riverbed (Wadi Batin/Kuwait River) that once flowed through Arabia - possibly the ancient Pishon.
